content:
Controversial "masculinist" influencer, 20-year-old Braden Peters (online alias Clavicular) is facing multiple criminal charges in the U.S. state of Massachusetts, including rape.

According to court records reviewed by HuffPost, Peters is charged with rape, engaging in sexual acts with a person rendered unconscious by drugs, and providing alcohol to a person under 21. The charges were filed earlier this month and first reported by The Bulwark, involving alleged incidents in May 2025. The influencer's attorney of record has not been publicly identified, but records show he is due in court on October 14.

Peters' representative Mitchell Jackson texted NBC News Monday night: "Braden Peters has not yet been personally served. The Bulwark, as always, is overstating things."

Following news of the charges, Peters posted multiple times on X, seemingly directed at a woman who had previously accused him.

He wrote Monday: "Every successful young man deals with this kind of thing — people want your money. Greed is evil." He attached a video from content creator Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, who sued him in April alleging assault, fraud, and sexual misconduct.

Details in that lawsuit overlap with the affidavit supporting Peters' recent criminal charges. The suit alleges Peters brought the then-under-21 TikTok star back to his parents' home on Cape Cod and provided her with "excessive" alcohol. It accuses Peters of "penetrating her and having sex with her" while she was too drunk to consent.

Mendoza's suit also alleges Peters injected her with Aqualyx — a fat-dissolving substance not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) — during a livestream.

Meanwhile, the criminal affidavit against Peters describes an incident on Cape Cod in which he allegedly instructed a 17-year-old, whose name is redacted, to lie on a livestream and say she was 18.

"He also instructed her to say the alcohol was water so his Twitch account and stream wouldn't get banned," the affidavit reads, adding that the alleged victim said she "felt peer-pressured into drinking it."

According to the affidavit, she told law enforcement that after the stream ended, the two were making out on a couch while she was "extremely drunk," and she eventually fell asleep in his bed. She said, however, that she awoke to find Peters "having sex with me."

The officer's report in the affidavit states: "She said because it was already happening, she did not tell Mr. Peters to stop." It adds that she "stated she did not consent to the sex acts."

In a statement to HuffPost, Jackson hinted that the woman filing the lawsuit is the same person described in the affidavit. The statement notes that the original version of the suit did not allege sexual assault.

"She did not include sexual assault as a charge when she filed the suit — that was added in an amendment months later," the statement reads.

He also added that Peters has "filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit" because he has evidence showing the accuser "knew exactly what was happening when Aqualyx was injected," and that she "went to the police" only after Peters "refused to pay her."
